$comment: §NEWLY-MEASURED (2026-08-12) — THE THIRD STATE. NOT DEBT. NOT A REGRESSION.
gate-debt.json declares exactly two states, and BIM 3.0 Phase 1 produces a third
one that fits neither:
• REGRESSION      — a gate fails and is NOT on gate-debt.json. Something got
WORSE. Blocks.
• DECLARED DEBT   — a gate is ON gate-debt.json. Somebody CHOSE to ship a known
contract violation (rule 3: never added without an explicit
founder/architect decision).
• NEWLY MEASURED  — THIS FILE. A gate that was BUILT THIS WEEK and lands RED on
defects that PREDATE it. Nothing got worse; the INSTRUMENT
ARRIVED. And nobody chose to ship these — they were never
measured, so there was no decision to make.
Filing a newly-measured gate under either existing label is a lie in a different
direction each way. Calling it a REGRESSION says the tree got worse on the day
someone wrote a scanner, which trains people to read red as noise — that is how
the whole suite ended up unwired in the first place (L-774). Calling it DECLARED
DEBT backdates a decision nobody made and quietly converts 'we have never looked
at this' into 'we accepted this', which is the §CONTEXT-DATA-HONESTY failure this
repository keeps paying for: two very different facts printing the same value.
─── WHY A SIBLING FILE AND NOT A SECTION INSIDE gate-debt.json ───────────────
Three reasons, in order of weight:
1. DIFFERENT CONSENT RULES. gate-debt.json rule 3 attaches a founder decision to
the ACT OF ADDING A LINE, because adding one there means choosing to ship a
known violation. This category's entries are the opposite act — choosing to
START MEASURING. Putting both under one roof means the strongest rule in that
file (rule 3) either leaks onto entries that should not need it, or gets
weakened to accommodate them. Rule 3 is left untouched and un-diluted by
keeping this out of that file entirely.
2. DIFFERENT SHAPE. gate-debt.json's `failing` is a bare `string[]` — a name and
nothing else. An entry here is meaningless without its pinned reading, its
exit condition and its review date. Bolting a structured array beside a flat
one in the same file gives readers of `failing` a partial view of what the
suite tolerates, which is exactly the shape of defect §3.20 K2 of
BIM30-READINESS-GATES names: one list that grows to fit whatever is failing.
3. TWO LISTS ARE AUDITABLE; ONE MERGED LIST IS NOT. The sizes of these two files
mean different things and must be readable separately. Declared debt going up
is bad news. This file going up is, on its face, GOOD news — it means more of
the estate is instrumented — right up until an entry expires unfixed.
─── DOES ADDING HERE NEED A FOUNDER DECISION? NO — WITH THREE HARD EDGES ─────
STATED EXPLICITLY BECAUSE THE ANSWER DIFFERS FROM RULE 3 AND MUST NOT BE INFERRED.
Adding a FIRST READING for a gate does NOT require a founder decision. Requiring
one would put a human approval step in front of TURNING AN INSTRUMENT ON, and the
predictable response to that friction is to not land the gate — which is precisely
what BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.3 forbids: *deferring a gate until its subject is
fixed is how a subject stays unfixed*. The founder's authority is over what we
SHIP, not over what we are ALLOWED TO KNOW. An entry here asserts no tolerance; it
asserts that a number has been written down and may now only fall.
The three edges, each of which IS a decision and therefore DOES need the founder:
(a) AN ENTRY MAY ONLY BE ADDED IN THE COMMIT THAT INTRODUCES ITS GATE. An entry
added later is not a first reading — the gate ran and something changed — so
it is either a regression or debt, and it goes through rule 3.
(b) RAISING A PINNED READING IS FORBIDDEN OUTRIGHT, founder or not. That is R7:
a measurement raised becomes a permission. The only legal edit to a reading
is downward.
(c) EXTENDING A `reviewBy`, OR MOVING AN ENTRY FROM THIS FILE TO gate-debt.json,
REQUIRES THE FOUNDER. That is the moment 'we have not fixed this yet' turns
into 'we are choosing to live with this', and it is exactly the decision
rule 3 exists to gate. This is the join between the two files, and it is
deliberately the only one.
─── THE RATCHET LIVES IN THE GATE, NOT IN THIS FILE ─────────────────────────
Every entry below is a gate that reports through the ONE exit-code implementation
at tools/rac-conformance/certification/contract.ts. That implementation already
returns 3 when findings exceed the declared level and 3 when a declared entry is
no longer measured. So:
exit 1 → at or below the pin. run-all absorbs it AS NEWLY-MEASURED.
exit 3 → the pin was exceeded, or the gate's own ledger is stale.
NEVER ABSORBED HERE. run-all's §RATCHET-EXCEEDED-IS-NEVER-DEBT branch
fires before this file is consulted, and it exits 1 for the suite.
This file therefore does NOT re-implement the ratchet, and must not: a second
comparator over the same number is a second thing that can disagree. `pinnedTo`
below is a POINTER to where the authoritative number lives plus a human-readable
copy of it — if the two ever disagree, THE GATE IS RIGHT and this file is stale.
─── TIME-BOUNDED, AND THE BOUND IS ENFORCED ─────────────────────────────────
Every entry carries `reviewBy`. run-all FAILS when today > reviewBy. That is the
whole point of the field: a category with no exit is how 'temporary' becomes
permanent, and a date nobody enforces is a comment. `reviewBy` is NOT a fix
deadline — it is the date by which the entry must be re-argued: fixed and struck,
or moved to gate-debt.json as an explicit founder decision to live with it. Both
outcomes are honest. Silently sitting here for a year is not.
─── PAID INSTRUMENT DEBT LEAVES THIS FILE TOO ───────────────────────────────
The gate-debt.json rule-2 discipline applies verbatim: an entry here whose gate
starts PASSING is a FAILURE of this file and run-all says so. Otherwise this rots
into a list of things that are secretly fine, which is the one failure mode both
ledgers share.
createdBecause: BIM 3.0 Phase 1 Tier 1 landed three gates RED on pre-existing production defects (BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.3), and gate-debt.json had no category that described them without lying.

predatesTheGate: F-C1 · RIVAL RECORD MINT loses properties SILENTLY. packages/sync-client/src/YjsDocAdapter.ts:690-700 (_applyDeclaredProperties) and :598-602 (applyCommand) both do get-or-create — read the element record, and if it is absent construct a new Y.Map and set it into the elements map under that id. Two PARTITIONED clients that each first-touch the same element therefore each mint a RIVAL Y.Map into the same key; on merge Yjs keeps ONE container and discards the other WITH EVERY PROPERTY INSIDE IT. Reproduced in ~20 lines with no harness involved. CONTROL proves it is the rival mint and not concurrency as such: the identical two edits on a record created once and replicated BEFORE the partition keep every value. P8-relevant: the loss emits NO CRDTConflict, because _discloseOverwrittenLocalWrites compares property VALUES, not rival CONTAINERS — so a property nobody concurrently edited disappears with no conflict raised anywhere.

F-C2 · UNDO CROSSES THE USER BOUNDARY. After client B's materialColor edit had been applied into client A's store, client A undoing ITS OWN height gesture reverted B's colour on A ('#c0ffee' before A's undo, '#aabbcc' after). C03 §4.5-4.8 makes undo per-gesture; one user's Ctrl+Z must never revert another user's work. The remote edit is applied through the bus as element.updateParameters, which the legacy CommandManager stack treats as ordinary local history.
F-C3 · A's undo did not revert A's own gesture in the same run (height stayed 5), so the undo stack is wrong in BOTH directions under concurrency, not merely over-broad.

F-C4 · read-leg-did-not-reach-store: after sync both Y.Docs agree on a value that at least one client's authoritative WallStore does not hold. Attributed by the gate: when the documents agree and the stores do not, the defect is in the read leg (ElementSyncReader → sink → bus), not in the merge.
entries.exitCondition: F-C1 green when a concurrent first-touch of the same element cannot destroy a property nobody edited — either by reconciling rival containers, or by refusing to mint a second one, or (P8) by emitting a CRDTConflict so the loss is at least DISCLOSED rather than silent. F-C2/F-C3 green when a remote-applied change does not enter the local undo history as a local gesture, so that A's undo reverts A's gesture and only A's. F-C4 green when a merged document value reaches the authoritative store on both clients. When maxFindings reaches 0 the gate is hard-0 and this entry is struck.

entries.residency: tools/rac-conformance/certification/gates/ per BIM30-READINESS-GATES §2.1a. The boundary test — does this gate need something that does not exist until something runs? — answers YES. Three of its five clauses drive live runtime state: the authority question is asked over rooms held in a REAL RoomStore, and the load-bearing clause DISPATCHES the real room.delete through the real CommandBus into the real plugins/rooms handler and the real window.commandManager bridge, then reads the store back to see what survived. A source scan cannot see a deletion; C75 §6.3(d) concedes exactly this about its own three static provenance gates, which is why E-13 exists.
entries.firstReading: exit 1 DECLARED-LEVEL — 7 findings against a declared level of 7. ALL TWELVE FLOORS MET, including four executed controls: the authority function returns three DISTINCT answers rather than one constant; the refusable clear does NOT refuse an all-system-produced set; a declared prior run yields determined and finds the survivor; and the clear loop actually removed rooms (an arm that deleted nothing would prove nothing about protection). The load-bearing measurement is clause (b): a level holding one AUTHORED room (detectionMethod=manual-boundary, what RoomTool stamps when a human draws) and one flood-filled room was put through the live §GRAPH-CLEAR-FIRST pattern — seeded=2, remaining=0, the authored room survived=FALSE. R8 names this defect and the gate reproduces it rather than describing it.
entries.pinnedTo: the `declared: 7` constant in the gate, with all seven findings NAMED in findingNames on every run. Checked in both directions by contract.ts: an eighth finding exits 3, and dropping to six without striking this entry also exits 3.
predatesTheGate: R8-a · PV-01 IS LIVE. `auto-topology` is simultaneously a real detection method (RoomDetectionEngine.ts:499) and the `|| auto-topology` deserialisation default at packages/room-topology/src/roomSnapshotUtils.ts:156, where an `as any` defeats the union at exactly the point that would have caught it. A room reading auto-topology is therefore ambiguous between flood-filled and origin-not-recorded, and no consumer can separate them. C75 §2.5 / PV-01.

R8-b · THE HOUSE EXECUTOR DESTROYS AUTHORED ROOMS, MEASURED. apps/editor/src/ui/house-layout/HouseLayoutExecutor.ts:1757-1766 (§GRAPH-CLEAR-FIRST) reads roomStore.getByLevel(levelId) UNFILTERED and dispatches room.delete for every id. Nothing consults provenance; the block comment asserts the rooms are "pre-existing (detection)" artefacts and cannot know that. The deletes are fire-and-forget (void, never awaited before BatchCreateRoomsCommand on the next line), the failure path is an empty catch, and the user is never told. A room the user drew is deleted silently. R8 exit condition, verbatim: "the house executor’s silent room deletion becomes a reported, refusable consequence."

R8-d · ALREADY-GENERATED AWARENESS IS NOT PERSISTED. generationId / generatedBy / isGenerated / sourceGenerator return ZERO first-party hits across packages/, plugins/ and apps/ (measured 2026-08-12). Generators carry only a command-level `source` label (HOUSE_GRAPH_ROOMS et al.) passed to cm.execute for undo/telemetry; it is never persisted onto the created elements, so nothing downstream can query which elements a generator produced. Consequence: HouseLayoutExecutor mints fresh levels per run with Date.now()+Math.random() ids and clears only ROOMS — walls, doors, windows, slabs, stairs, roofs, furniture and lighting from a previous run are never removed, so a second run stacks a whole building on the first.

R8-e1 · NOT EVALUATED — authored wall byte-intact. No wall carries provenance; every `origin:` in packages/schemas/src/elements/*.ts is a geometric Vec3 (C75 §0 Finding 2, re-measured and still true). An authored wall is indistinguishable from a generated one at HEAD, so the verification has no subject.
R8-e2 · NOT EVALUATED — authored opening byte-intact / generated opening revalidated. Doors and windows carry no provenance either, and no regeneration pass over openings exists to run.

R8-e3 · NOT EVALUATED — generated wall UPDATED by the regeneration. There is NO *.regenerate verb in the repository. Only GENERATE_STAIR_GEOMETRY (one stair from its params) and ai.floorplan.generate exist; neither regenerates an area over mixed provenance. The house/apartment generators are not bus verbs at all — they are UI controllers (houseLayoutTrigger.ts / HouseLayoutController.ts), which is precisely why no verb can enforce clear-then-rebuild centrally.

R8-e4 · NOT EVALUATED — the AI-proposed element still marked INFERRED. No AI-proposed element persists an origin; ai.floorplan.generate stamps nothing on what it creates. Compounded by R7’s own declared finding that no production call site builds a CommandExecutionContext at all.
entries.positiveControlNote: FOUR controls run every invocation and are FLOORS, not prose. (1) DISCRIMINATION — mayRegenerate must return three DISTINCT kinds across an authored, a system-produced and a provenance-less element; a function hard-wired to any single answer would satisfy one assertion and is caught here. (2) NEGATIVE — planRegenerationClear over two system-produced rooms must NOT refuse, so refuse=true in the main arm is a decision rather than a constant. (3) UNDETERMINED-IS-A-READING — queryPriorGeneration with a declared run must return determined and correctly split stillPresent from gone, so the undetermined verdict in the no-memory case is not a stub. (4) TEETH — the clear loop must actually have removed rooms from the real store; an arm where nothing was deleted cannot testify about what survived, and exits 2 rather than reporting protection.
entries.exitCondition: Per finding. R8-a is struck when roomSnapshotUtils.ts:156 records UNKNOWN-with-reason instead of the `|| auto-topology` default and the serialised field is typed RoomDetectionMethod rather than bare string (roadmap Phase 8 change 2). R8-b is struck when §GRAPH-CLEAR-FIRST consults planRegenerationClear (or an equivalent authority check) before deleting, surfaces the refusal to the user, and this gate’s clause (b) measures the authored room SURVIVING — at which point clause (b) flips from a finding to a floor. R8-d is struck when elements carry a persisted generation marker and queryPriorGeneration reads it rather than a caller’s in-process declaration. R8-e1..e4 are struck one at a time as their substrate lands (Phase 8 element field; a *.regenerate bus verb), and each strike REPLACES a NOT-EVALUATED line with a real executed arm — the NOT_EVALUATED floor of 4 must be LOWERED deliberately in the same commit, never left to drift. When all seven are struck the gate is hard-0 and this entry leaves the ledger.
entries.territory: The gate and apps/editor/src/engine/provenance/ElementProvenanceIndex.ts are new files. The gate IMPORTS but never edits packages/schemas/src/provenance (the L0 vocabulary), packages/room-topology (RoomStore, RoomTypes) and plugins/rooms (DeleteRoomHandler) — the landed precedent of check-approval-binding importing plugins/wall read-only.
entries.cannotSee: FIVE named blind spots. (1) The §GRAPH-CLEAR-FIRST loop in clause (b) is TRANSCRIBED from HouseLayoutExecutor.ts:1757-1766, not imported — the executor is a 254 KB UI class requiring a full runtime, and it was another agent’s live territory when this gate landed. The gate therefore proves the PATTERN destroys authored rooms, not that this exact executor instance does; this is its weakest link and is stated in the gate header. (2) Provenance for walls, doors, windows, slabs and every non-room element — there is no field to read, which is finding R8-e1/e2. (3) Whether a REGENERATION preserves prior provenance (C75 §2.7 replaced chain) — no regeneration verb exists to run. (4) The export boundary: how AUTHORED/OBSERVED/COMPUTED/INFERRED/REGENERATED land in IFC and DXF is C75 §5 / PV-04, UNPROVEN and untouched here. (5) The BROWSER half — whether a human running the house generator in a live browser sees a refusal, since the refusable form is not yet wired into the executor.
entries.notImplementedHere: This gate does NOT claim review §6’s six-element scenario passes. THREE of its seven verifications are executed (an authored element is protected, a system-produced one is clearable, and a report names which and why); FOUR are printed as NOT EVALUATED with the reason and the substrate that would close each. E-13 asked for the scenario to be "named now, RED, per the roadmap’s own §0.1 rule (a gate lands before its implementation, and lands RED)" — that is exactly what this is. Reading its exit code as scenario coverage would be the C70 §8.i capability claim the whole suite exists to prevent.
